newsitem.title: USA: UAL confident, but Wall Street less sure.
newsitem.headline: UAL confident, but Wall Street less sure.

text.p: UAL Corp recently painted a rosy picture for fiscal 1997, but some analysts are less optimistic.
Gruntal & Co said on Thursday it trimmed its "enthusiastic" forecast of UAL Corp's fiscal 1997 earnings to $8.50 from $9, partly because of the cost of improved services.
Analysts on average estimate UAL's 1997 earnings at $7.72 a share, according to First Call.
For the 1996 full year, analysts expect UAL to earn $7.69 a share, compared with $5.13 in 1995.
Gruntal analyst Steve Lewins said the firm continued to rate the stock as "outperform" in light of an upbeat presentation made by the company in a meeting with airline analysts on Wednesday.

In that meeting, UAL, the parent of United Airlines, predicted improved profitability and three percent capacity growth. The company also said it expected its results in 1997 to be "even better" than its 1996 performance.
The carrier also said it expected its domestic unit revenue growth to surpass the industry average.
"They were more ambitious on the revenue side than the Street (estimates)," said Glenn Engel, an airline analyst with Goldman Sachs, who attended the meeting.
UAL also touted the tentative pact it reached with its pilots, saying the agreement would bring wages back to industry levels.
Despite UAL's optimism, Engel questioned whether the airline would realize any substantial long-term savings out of the deal.
The U.S. airline industry posted record results in the first nine months of 1996, after losing $13 billion over the first half of the decade.
Still, maintaining the record pace could prove difficult for an industry that will likely show only moderate capacity growth over the next year, analysts said.
"The market seems to think that this is as good as it's going to get," Engel said. "There's some risk in airline stocks right now."
UAL closed at 59-3/4, down 1/8, in trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
